To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of bcl-2 protein is significantly increased in Kaposi’s Sarcoma, and the expression of the p53 protein is significantly increased as well.

bcl-2 is expressed at a low level in the early patch stage, and increases with progression of KS to the plaque and nodular stages, while p53 is not expressed in early stages but is expressed in 54% of the late nodular stage.
the immunoexpression of bcl-2 increases with progression from patch to plaque and nodular stages, and p53 is not expressed in patch and plaque stages but expressed in 54.16 of nodular stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemistry of bcl-2, p53 and Ki-67 in Kaposi’s Sarcoma (KS).
the immunoexpression of bcl-2 in the different sub-types of KS, and the role of p53 in the evolution of the disease.
the expression of bcl-2 protein and p53 in the different histological stages of Kaposi sarcoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a progressive increase in bcl-2 immunostaining and a progressive increase in p53 immunostaining from the patch stage through to the nodular stages.
bcl-2 is a useful marker for KS and that p53 is not expressed in the earlier stages of KS, but is upregulated in the nodular form of KS.
bcl-2 expression is a late phenomenon in KS, while p53 expression occurs in the nodular form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a progressive increase in bcl-2 immnoprofile from the patch stage to the plaque stage to the nodular one, whereas p53 is not expressed in the first 2 stages but is expressed in 54.16 % of the nodular cases.
bcl-2 expression is a marker for the late stage of KS.

there is a significant difference in bcl-2 immuostaining between the different histological stages of KS, but there is no significant difference in the immunoexpression of p53 between the different histologic stages of KS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunoprofile of KS is dependent on the histological subtype and that bcl-2 is expressed in all subtypes while p53 is expressed only in the nodular subtype.
the immunoprofile of bcl-2 in the different stages of KS is a good prognostic indicator.
bcl-2 expression in KS is a late event and that it may be a marker for the progression to nodular KS.
